rounds.text: The long-term fundamental performance of Manali Petrochemicals is concerning, as the company has delivered stagnant sales growth of 0% over the last five years and a contraction of 5% over the last three years [E15, E16]. Profitability metrics remain persistently weak, with a return on equity of only 6% and a return on capital employed of 7.2% [E12, E13]. These figures significantly underperform sector benchmarks, which stand at 7.72% for ROE and 9.53% for ROCE [E9, E10]. Furthermore, the quality of recent earnings is questionable, as they include a substantial other income component of Rs 122 Cr [E64]. While the stock is currently trading near its 52-week high, investors should note the historical volatility, which includes a massive peak-to-trough drawdown of 82.6% and high annualised volatility of 58.9% [E54, E55]. Conceded: the company maintains a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.11x and has seen a recent surge in operating margins [E30, E38].
